explanation: Willis cites Fourth Circuit Lundy (noting only cert. granted) for general § 6511 refund-claim timing in a bankruptcy appeal, against the taxpayers; it does not rely on the rejected three-year § 6512(b)(3)(B) Tax Court look-back holding.

Eleventh Circuit Kimel held the ADEA did not abrogate immunity, which the Supreme Court affirmed (own knowledge); Garrett on remand cites Kimel only as history for the ADA point and applies the Supreme Court's Garrett reversal.

Waddell fixes RICO accrual using Bath's injury-plus-pattern discovery rule, the rule Rotella rejected, flagging Bath only as overruled on other grounds by Lampf; Rotella is not mentioned in the text given.
Armstrong states and applies an overt-act element for § 1956(h) conspiracy citing Wilson, the Fifth Circuit rule Whitfield rejected, and the text given never mentions Whitfield.

Everett held intent to defraud or expose the bank itself is unnecessary, consistent with Loughrin (own knowledge); Nazzal cites it only for general § 1344 elements and the sufficiency standard, not the § 1344(2) bank-intent question.

Mullican relies on Ludwig's request-required, no-duty-to-advise rule without citing Flores-Ortega; but Flores-Ortega rejected the opposite per se rule (First/Ninth Circuits), so Ludwig was not on the rejected side, though its no-duty statement is qualified (own knowledge).

Galvez-Letona states, citing J.L./Share Ourselves, that Congress unequivocally authorized damages against federal agencies under § 504, the answer Lane rejected, without mentioning Lane; caveat: only equitable relief and fees were sought, so the damages statement is dictum.
